newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Monday, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Cattle owners were asking $67.00 per cwt, but no bids were reported, they said. Packer buyers reportedly were out looking at this week's showlists, but not showing any aggressiveness.
"They're taking it real slow this morning. Part of it could be the weather," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Temperatures in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area remained in single digits amid light snow.
Cold weather over the weekend reportedly slowed weight gains in cattle, but was not severe enough to stress the livestock or draw them off feed, cattle feeders said.
Conditions improved over the weekend when strong winds subsided, they said.
"They're not gaining as they should, but overall, they're holding up pretty well," a Panhandle source said.
Light snow fell during the weekend in Kansas and the Panhandle, and outside of making some country roads slick, the snow was not expected to hurt the cattle further, sources said.
